body: Hello Cython community. I wanted to take a stab at [this issue](https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/3696) as it looks like it hasn't ben addressed yet. Hoping the build CI passes and if not someone can point me in the right direction perhaps? Tried running tests locally but got a syntax error from `Shadow.py`

comment_data.body:
I don't think these are necessary (or at least they seem tangential to the main purpose of the PR).

I think these are used for calculation of constant expressions. In that case we have a `BinopNode` with `inplace=True` and an operator without the `=`.

I don't think the C++ operators that this PR is about should contribute to constant expressions.

comment_data.body:
Is there a reason not to do the full list of inplace C++ operators?

```
^=
&=
|=
>>=
<<=
```

I think all of the extra ones I've listed are also part of Python.

(If there is a reason then I'm happy to skip them)

As best as I can tell, this file is now unused and should probably just be deleted. At very least there's nothing to be gained from adding to it.

_edit:_ file is now deleted in master branch...
These should be an error I think? They don't make much sense

comment_data.body:
It doesn't look like these are ever used in the test.

At very least I think we'd want to know from the tests that Cython is calling `+=` rather than `_ = _ + _`.

Note that I don't think you can usefully use the return value because `a = (b += 2)` isn't valid Python code (although is valid c++ code)

comment_data.body:
To me it doesn't look like this is generating the code that you're claiming it's generating (just by doing `python3 runtests.py cpp_operator_exc_handling --no-cleanup` and looking at `TEST_TMP/run/cpp/cpp_operator_exc_handling/cpp_operator_exc_handling.cpp`)

To test it from the behaviour I'd make the in place operators raise on a different exception value (not 4) and then you'd be able to tell that you're calling the right code.
